interactions.description: Together they raise the risk of serious bleeding, and NSAIDs also irritate the stomach lining.
Aspirin adds to warfarin’s blood-thinning effect and raises bleeding risk.
Together they raise the risk of serious bleeding, and NSAIDs also irritate the stomach lining.
Ciprofloxacin can raise warfarin levels (higher INR), increasing bleeding risk.
Amiodarone can strongly raise warfarin levels. Close monitoring is usually needed.
Some antibiotics increase warfarin’s effect. INR monitoring is often advised.
Regular, higher-dose acetaminophen use can raise INR.
SSRIs can add to bleeding risk when taken with warfarin.
Ibuprofen can interfere with aspirin’s heart-protective effect, and both raise stomach bleeding risk.
Two NSAIDs together add side effects (stomach bleeding, kidney strain) without extra benefit.
NSAIDs can weaken the blood-pressure effect and strain the kidneys.

SSRIs plus NSAIDs raise the risk of stomach and other bleeding.
NSAIDs can raise lithium to toxic levels.
NSAIDs can raise methotrexate levels and increase its toxicity.
Both raise the risk of bleeding.
Sometimes prescribed on purpose, but it raises bleeding risk. Follow your prescriber’s plan.
Both raise the risk of bleeding.
Both raise potassium. High potassium can cause dangerous heart rhythm problems.
ACE inhibitors can raise lithium levels.
Can cause a sudden, severe drop in blood pressure. Never combine.
Clarithromycin greatly raises simvastatin levels, increasing the risk of muscle damage.
Clarithromycin raises statin levels and the risk of muscle problems.
Amlodipine raises simvastatin levels. The simvastatin dose is usually capped.
Risk of serotonin syndrome (agitation, fever, fast heartbeat) and seizures.

Amiodarone raises digoxin levels, risking toxicity.
Verapamil raises digoxin levels and can slow the heart rate.
Together they can slow the heart too much and drop blood pressure.
Calcium reduces levothyroxine absorption. Doses are usually spaced about 4 hours apart.
Less stomach acid may slightly lower levothyroxine absorption.
Calcium binds ciprofloxacin and reduces absorption. Spacing the doses is usually advised.
Fluoroquinolones can cause blood sugar swings in people taking diabetes medicines.
Omeprazole can reduce clopidogrel’s activation, making it less effective.
Penicillins can slow methotrexate clearance and raise its levels.
